question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 65 minutes and 26 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 30 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take total work = LCM(65,26) = 130

A = 2 units/min, B = 5 units/min

A works 30 min ⇒ work = 60 units

Remaining = 130 − 60 = 70 units ⇒ done by B

Time = 70 ÷ 5 = 14 min

**∴ Answer = 14 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A fills in 65 min, Pipe B fills in 26 min

Total time = 30 min

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let B works for x minutes

⇒ Work by A in 30 min = 30 × 2 = 60 units

⇒ Work by B in x min = 5x units

⇒ Total work = 130 units

⇒ 60 + 5x = 130

⇒ 5x = 70

⇒ x = 14

**∴ The correct answer is 14 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Taking LCM converts fractions into whole numbers for easy solving.

Efficiency Concept

Efficiency = Work done per minute.

Partial Work

One pipe may stop earlier, so split work accordingly.
